entries.title: Gatherings renamed to Field Events across the UI
entries.summary: The module previously called **Gatherings** is now labelled **Field Events** everywhere an organizer reads it: the sidebar nav, the event-type picker, breadcrumbs, tab labels, settings pages, email designer, registration form editor, Early Access catalogue card, Apps catalogue, and all empty/error states. URLs have also moved from `/org/:orgId/gatherings/…` to `/org/:orgId/field-events/…`. The underlying data kind (`gathering`) and feature flags are unchanged.

enable.path: Get started → Early Access → Preview → Field Events

entries.use_case: Customers who run satellite events, roadshows, or on-site activations alongside their main conference will now see the module labelled **Field Events**, which more clearly describes what it is for than the previous name.

cs_action.note: Pure display rename; no data migration, no flag changes needed. Old /gatherings/ URLs no longer work — there are no redirects — but the feature was not yet in use by customers.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Any time a customer asks about the Gatherings module or sees it in Early Access.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers running satellite or field events alongside a main conference.
internal.gotchas: Old /org/:orgId/gatherings/… bookmarks or hardcoded links will 404 — no redirects were added. The feature flag id remains 'gatherings', so Early Access toggles and internal tooling are unaffected.
internal.talk_track: The module is the same product you may have seen as Gatherings; it has been renamed Field Events to better reflect how customers use it for roadshows and satellite activations.

draft.docs_gap: The glossary and any guide that references "Gatherings" as a module name should be updated to say "Field Events" throughout.
draft.why_use_it: Field Events let you manage smaller, standalone gatherings — roadshows, satellite events, on-site activations — inside the same Sessionboard organization as your main conference. Each field event gets its own agenda, registration, emails, pages, and settings, so your team works in one place without mixing data across programs.

entries.title: Advocacy for exhibitors and sponsors without the portal: email, export and an open link for Groups campaigns
entries.summary: A Groups campaign now has a **Share** tab. **Email exhibitors their links** sends every contact of every company on the campaign their own link to the company's card; **Export personal links (CSV)** gives one row per person at each company; and the **Open link** lets anyone at a company on the campaign enter their name, email and company to get the company's card. **Copy magic link** works on a company's row, and the card's role stamp (“Exhibiting at …” / “Proud sponsor of …”) drives the default share message. Nobody needs an Exhibitor portal login. Groups campaigns, the email, the export and the open link work on every plan; Exhibitor Pro or Sponsor Pro is needed only to target **By portal** or to show the campaign inside a portal.

enable.path: Marketing → Advocacy → Groups campaign → Share → Open link (the email and export need nothing turned on)

where.path: Marketing → Advocacy → Groups campaign → Share tab; Recipients tab → Copy magic link

entries.use_case: Exhibitors and sponsors post that they are at your event from a link in their inbox or your exhibitor newsletter, with no portal to log into — the same portal-free toolkit attendees got, now for companies.

cs_action.note: Customers training exhibitors on Advocacy this month (IAAPA Expo 2026, event 6102) should use the Share tab instead of the Exhibitor portal path. Needs the web-api release carrying lennd/sessionboard-web-api#4774 (migration adds Amplify_Recipient_Magic_Tokens.contact_id).

internal.when_to_bring_up: Any customer running a sponsor or exhibitor Advocacy campaign, or complaining that exhibitors never log into the portal.
internal.who_should_get_it: Trade-show and expo organizers (IAAPA, Informa, Clarion shows) and anyone with sponsor Advocacy campaigns.
internal.staff_path: Event → Marketing → Advocacy → open a Groups campaign → Share
internal.gotchas: The people emailed are the company's contacts on the event (Account_Contacts + Event_Module_Records) — a company with no contacts is reported, not emailed. The open link never creates a company: the visitor's company must already be on the campaign. A known CRM email is emailed its own link rather than shown the card. Exported CSV gains a Company column. The Groups tile is no longer greyed out without a Pro module (web-ui-v2 #1194); only the By portal targeting button is.
internal.talk_track: Your exhibitors don't need a login. Send them their link, or drop the open link in the exhibitor newsletter, and every booth team can post that they're exhibiting with your tracked link.

entries.title: Credit Claiming attendance import accepts session codes as shown
entries.summary: The attendance CSV import in **Credit Claiming** now matches a session code exactly as Sessionboard displays it, with the event's prefix (for example `SESS-81`), as well as the bare number. Before, those rows failed with "No session of this event matches that session id or code."

where.path: Program → After the event → Credit Claiming → Attendance → Upload CSV

entries.use_case: Organizers copying session codes from the session list into an attendance file from their scanning vendor no longer have to strip the SESS- prefix first; every row imports on the first try.

cs_action.note: Automatic; re-upload any file whose rows failed on the prefix.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer says their attendance CSV import reports "No session of this event matches" for every row.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events in the Credit Claiming beta that import attendance by CSV.
internal.staff_path: Program → After the event → Credit Claiming → Attendance
internal.gotchas: Only the event's own prefix is stripped (case-insensitive, hyphen optional); an exact client session id still matches first. The time-zone half of this PR's title ships with web-ui-v2 #1175 and gets its own entry.
internal.talk_track: Paste the session code straight from Sessionboard into the attendance file — with or without SESS- — and the import matches it.

entries.title: Confirmation-page embed: works with no registrant id and shows a preview of the attendee's card from your merge fields
entries.summary: The **advocacy-attending** embed no longer needs a registrant id to be useful. With only the campaign id it shows the open-link signup form. Seed it with the registrant's first name, last name, company, job title and a photo (`avatar-url`) from your confirmation page's merge fields and it opens with a **preview of their card** — event logo, photo or initials, name, title, "I'm attending" — above the form, updating as they type. The photo is saved as the attendee's headshot when they click **Make my card**, so the real card has their face from the first render.

enable.path: Marketing → Advocacy → Attendees campaign → Share → Embed on your confirmation page → Signup form (open link); add avatar-url and the name/title/company attributes to the snippet

where.path: Your registration platform's confirmation page (the embed snippet from the campaign's Share tab)

entries.cs: Customers whose registration platform has no stable registrant id on the confirmation page (or who cannot pass it) can still show a personalized card: use the signup-form embed with the name, company, title and photo merge fields. Needs the campaign's Open link on. Reference setup: IAAPA Expo 2026 (event 6102).
entries.use_case: An attendee lands on the thank-you page and sees a card that already has their name, title, company and photo on it, with one button to make it theirs and post it, even though the registration platform never handed us an id.

cs_action.note: Nothing to enable. The seeded preview and avatar-url need the embeds PROD publish (lennd/sessionboard-embeds#122) and the web-api release carrying lennd/sessionboard-web-api#4782; until both are live the published script shows the prefilled form without the preview and ignores avatar-url.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer says their registration platform's confirmation page has no registrant id, or asks how to show a personalized card without a synced or imported attendee list.
internal.who_should_get_it: Organizers on Cvent, Swoogo, Swapcard, Bizzabo or an in-house registration site who send attendees to a confirmation page they control.
internal.staff_path: Event → Marketing → Advocacy → Attendees campaign → Share → Embed on your confirmation page → Signup form (open link)
internal.gotchas: Needs the campaign's Open link on. avatar-url must be an https image URL; javascript:, data: and relative values are ignored (initials show instead). The preview is drawn in the page from the seeds, not rendered by the template; the real card appears after Make my card. An email already on the attendee list still gets Check your inbox, never a card on the page. The photo is copied off the external host by a background job, so the Creator console may show the external URL for a minute.
internal.talk_track: Drop one snippet on your thank-you page and every registrant sees their own card, with their photo, before they click anything, even if your platform never gives us an id.

entries.title: Docusign contracts sent to sponsor/exhibitor accounts now resolve the signer from the account's primary contact
entries.summary: When sending a Docusign contract whose subject is an account (sponsor, exhibitor, or partner), Sessionboard now automatically resolves the signer from the account's primary contact — no manual recipient entry required. If the account has exactly one primary contact for the event (or org-level as a fallback), that person becomes the envelope recipient and their details fill any **Contact** template variables. If there are multiple primary contacts, the send is blocked with a message naming each candidate and prompting the organizer to choose one in **Review & edit fields**; if there is no primary contact, the error clearly states that no primary contact was found.

where.path: Sponsors or Exhibitors → [account record] → Contracts → Send via Docusign

entries.use_case: Organizers sending Docusign contracts to sponsors or exhibitors no longer need to type a recipient manually — as long as the account has one primary contact, the envelope goes straight to them. When the account has multiple primary contacts, the error message names each candidate so the organizer knows exactly who to choose.

cs_action.note: Behaviour change is automatic for all Docusign contract sends where the subject is an account. Previously these always failed with a 400 unless the admin typed a recipient; now they succeed when there is exactly one primary contact. Live in production since web-api release/2026-10-28 (2026-10-28 18:11 UTC).

internal.when_to_bring_up: Any time a customer reports that Docusign contracts to sponsors or exhibitors fail with a missing signer error, or when onboarding customers who use the sponsor/exhibitor pipeline with Docusign.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using Docusign contracts with sponsor, exhibitor, or partner account subjects.
internal.staff_path: Event → Sponsors or Exhibitors → account record → Contracts
internal.gotchas: The fix only resolves a signer when the account has exactly one primary contact. Accounts with two or more primary contacts will receive a 400 naming the candidates; accounts with none will receive a 400 saying no primary contact was found. Admins must designate a single primary contact or manually pick a recipient in Review & Edit.
internal.talk_track: Docusign contracts sent to sponsor or exhibitor accounts now automatically use the account's primary contact as the signer, so your team doesn't have to type a recipient every time. If an account has more than one primary contact, the system tells you exactly who they are so you can choose.

draft.docs_gap: The Docusign guide should document how account-subject contracts resolve the signer from the primary contact, including the event-scoped vs. org-level fallback logic and what happens when there are zero or multiple primary contacts.

entries.title: The Docusign app page shows its real connection state and describes contracts, not a program sync
entries.summary: **Apps → Docusign** no longer shows a **Coming soon** badge or copy about syncing your program. The tile and the app page now describe what Docusign does in Sessionboard — sending speaker, sponsor and exhibitor agreements from the record with Sessionboard variables, tracking the signature, and storing the signed PDF — and show **Connected** / **Connect Docusign** from your organization's real Docusign connections. The **Learn more** link opens the Docusign integration guide.
entries.use_case: Organizers evaluating Docusign for contracts see the real feature on the Apps page and can connect from there, instead of a Coming soon tile that described a program sync Docusign never did.

cs_action.note: Cosmetic plus the connect state. Live in production since the web-ui-v2 prod publish of 2026-10-28 18:23 UTC (sha 58117bc27d).

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks what the Docusign app in Apps does, or says it shows Coming soon.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every organization — the page is visible to all; connecting still needs the Contracts feature.

entries.title: Event home: every included tool on the dashboard, the board dashboard for everyone, and Registration in Early Access
entries.summary: The **Today** tab on every event now opens with **Your toolkit**: two rows of tiles, one per tool your event comes with, that scroll sideways. Tools you use show **In use** with a live count; included tools you have not set up show **Ready to start** with one set-up button; tools in Early Access show **Preview** or **Beta** and act through the program (**Join Early Access**, **Turn on preview**, **Request beta**, then **Requested**). **Tools / Timeline** switches to a Before / Event days / After view with the current phase highlighted and one **Next for you** pick. The board-style dashboard (**Needs you**, headline tiles, Submission Pacing, Recent submissions) is now on for every event; the old stat cards, disclosures tile and **Also check** line are gone. **Registration** is a Beta card in Early Access with **Request access**, and the last tile in the toolkit.

where.path: Event → Dashboard → Today → Your toolkit; Preview (Early Access) → Registration

entries.use_case: Organizers who never found Transcriptions, Advocacy, Clips or Galleries three levels down the sidebar see them on the event home with one button to start, and can request Beta features such as Registration from the same place.

cs_action.note: The board dashboard is now on for all customers — accounts that were previously v1-only will see the new board layout. Proactively check in with any customers who relied on the v1 stat cards, disclosures tile, or 'Also check' strip, as those are removed. Registration Beta tile is a good conversation starter for accounts asking about registration.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Any time a customer says they didn't know they had a tool, or when discussing upsell of Registration, Transcriptions, or Advocacy.
internal.who_should_get_it: All event organizers; especially valuable for customers who have been using only the Program module and are unaware of Marketing tools.
internal.gotchas: The v1 dashboard band (stat cards, disclosures tile, 'Also check' line, v1 pacing and recent tables inside Submission Forms) is removed for everyone. Only Submissions, Speakers, Agenda, Advocacy, Transcriptions, Clips and Galleries carry live counts until web-ui-v2 #1201 ships; other tiles read 'Ready to start' even when used. The Registration tile stays Beta until the Registration module is promoted (its access hook still requires staff). Transcriptions copy is deliberately audio-only: never say stream video.
internal.talk_track: Your event home now shows every tool you already own in one place — you can see what's active, what's ready to turn on, and request access to anything in Early Access like Registration, all without leaving the event.

draft.docs_gap: Closed: the Event Dashboard guide now documents Your toolkit, the Tools / Timeline toggle, Needs you, the headline tiles and the Early Access actions per tile, with new screenshots.
draft.why_use_it: The event home gives you a single place to see every tool included in your Sessionboard plan, track which ones are active, and turn on or request access to those you haven't tried yet. Live counts on each tile show real activity — submissions, speakers, transcripts, clips — so you can gauge adoption at a glance. The Tools / Timeline toggle lets you switch between a full tool inventory and a phase-aware checklist that highlights what to focus on before, during, and after the event.

entries.title: Get an email when a session is withdrawn, a file is uploaded or a portal task is completed
entries.summary: Three admin alerts that only reached the bell can now come by email: **Session Withdrawn**, **Session File Uploaded** and **Portal Task Completed**. Email is off for these until you tick it in **Notifications → Preferences**, so nobody's inbox changes on its own, and the column switch in the header leaves them alone. **Portal Task Completed** now names who completed which task, and it moved from the **Portal** group to **Admin**.
entries.use_case: Event teams that hand speaker uploads to an AV team, follow up on withdrawals, or chase portal tasks can get those alerts by email the moment they happen (or in the daily summary) instead of checking the bell.

cs_action.note: Opt-in per person; nothing changes for anyone until they tick Email.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks to be emailed when a speaker withdraws, uploads session files, or completes a portal task (Community ideas with 10, 15 and 8 votes).
internal.who_should_get_it: Event admins who coordinate AV files, withdrawals or portal task follow-up.
internal.staff_path: Event → Notifications → Preferences → Admin group → Email column
internal.gotchas: Email is deliberately opt-in: on by default it would have sent about 161,000 task-completed emails a quarter in the US. The column and category master switches skip these three cells. An older UI on the new API would show the cells ticked while nothing is sent, so the UI shipped first.
internal.talk_track: Tick Email on Session Withdrawn, Session File Uploaded or Portal Task Completed in your notification preferences and you'll get those by email, immediately or in your daily summary.

entries.title: File requests show who uploaded each file and link the session
entries.summary: Each revision on a file request now says who uploaded it, with their email, and marks an upload made by someone on your event team as **admin**. **Last uploaded by** sits at the top of the details. On a request attached to sessions, a **Session** row links straight to the session instead of repeating its title under **Submitted By**.
entries.use_case: When a file comes in for a session, you can see whether the speaker or a colleague uploaded it and jump to the session, rather than guessing the uploader from the presentation title.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks who uploaded a file to a file request, or can't tell a speaker's upload from one an organizer made for them.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every event using file requests, especially session-scoped ones.
internal.staff_path: Event → Portals → File Requests → open a request → open a record → Revision History
internal.gotchas: About 10% of US revisions in the last year were uploaded by an event team member on the participant's behalf; those now read Uploaded by admin. A deleted account shows Unknown.
internal.talk_track: Open a file request record and each revision now says who uploaded it, with their email, and session requests link straight to the session.

entries.title: Choose the columns in the Sessions Summary merge tag
entries.summary: The **Sessions Summary** merge tag now takes options, so you can drop or pick its columns. `{{{sessions_summary:exclude=status,session_id}}}` leaves out status and session ID; `{{{sessions_summary:include=title,starts_at,track}}}` shows exactly those columns in that order. Track, Format, Level, Language, Location, Tags and any Sessions field by name are available. The plain tag still renders the same six-column table as before.
entries.use_case: Organizers who email participants a list of their sessions can leave out internal columns such as status and session ID, or add the track and room, without building a separate template.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer does not want status or session ID in the Sessions Summary table (Community idea, 7 votes), or wants track or location in it.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers who email speakers, moderators or chairpersons from Contacts.
internal.staff_path: Event → Contacts → select → Send Emails → insert Sessions Summary, then edit the tag
internal.gotchas: The modal that builds the options for you (web-ui-v2 #1186) is super-user only for now; customers type the options into the tag. Unknown columns are ignored, and an include that names nothing known falls back to the default table. The Customize modal that builds the options with a live preview (lennd/sessionboard-web-ui-v2#1186) is super-user-only until promoted; typed options work for every admin.
internal.talk_track: Add exclude= or include= to the Sessions Summary tag to choose which columns your participants see.

entries.title: Send Email: a clear wait message when you hit the sending limit, and a limit that fits real use
entries.summary: When **Send Email** is rate-limited, the **Review** and **Send** steps now say **You have sent a lot of emails in a short time. Please wait about N minutes and try again.** instead of the misleading "We could not build a preview" error; the minutes come from the server (or "a few minutes" when unknown). The limit itself was widened: it is now counted per event, building a preview no longer spends the sending budget, and the allowance is 300 per 15 minutes — several times faster than anyone can click Review → Send — so an admin sending invitations one session at a time, or a team behind one office network, is no longer stopped after ten sends.

where.path: Speakers (or Contacts) → Send Email → Review / Send

entries.use_case: An organizer sending moderator invitations one session at a time no longer hits a wall after ten sends, and when a team really does send a great deal at once the dialog says how long to wait instead of blaming their recipient selection.

cs_action.note: No action needed; the fix is default-on and purely changes error copy.

internal.when_to_bring_up: If a customer reports a confusing 'could not build a preview' error when sending emails to a large list.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any organizer who sends high-volume email batches and may hit the rate limit.
internal.staff_path: Event → Speakers or Contacts → Send Email → Review or Send step
internal.gotchas: The wait time shown is rounded up from the Retry-After header; if the header is absent the message says 'a few minutes'. The new limit is 300 previews and 300 sends per event per 15 minutes, with a 1,000-request-per-15-minute ceiling per IP address across events as a flood guard. SB-10516 (CES 2027, event 6815).
internal.talk_track: Sending one email at a time used to stop after about ten with a confusing 'could not build a preview' error. The limit is now generous and per event, and if you ever do hit it the dialog tells you exactly how many minutes to wait.

entries.title: Download the Ready Room desktop app from inside Sessionboard
entries.summary: A **Download Ready Room** card on the **Live Transcribe** page and at the top of the Live Transcribe Console home offers the installer for your operating system first — macOS, Windows, or Windows on ARM — with the other builds, a checksums link and the version beside it. Links are made when the page opens and work for 15 minutes; the card appears only while a release is published.

where.path: Marketing → Live Transcribe (Download Ready Room card); Live Transcribe Console home

entries.use_case: A/V operators and event admins no longer need to hunt for a separate download page — the correct version of the Ready Room desktop app is always one click away from the Live Transcribe setup screen, with links that expire after 15 minutes for security.

cs_action.note: The download card only appears once the S3 bucket is provisioned and a release is published. Until the infrastructure follow-up (IaaC) is complete, the card will be hidden (available: false). Confirm with engineering before telling customers the download is live.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer is setting up Live Transcribe and asks how their A/V crew gets the desktop app.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using Live Transcribe with an on-site A/V crew running Ready Room.
internal.gotchas: Download links are presigned and expire after 15 minutes — send the crew to the page, not the link. The card is invisible until the S3 bucket exists and a release has been published (the API returns available: false otherwise). Requires S3_BUCKET_READY_ROOM_RELEASES in Doppler per environment. Ready Room is the desktop twin of the browser Console: same audio capture, same sessions.
internal.talk_track: Your A/V team can now download the Ready Room app straight from the Live Transcribe setup page — no separate link to share, and the download is authenticated so only your team can access it.

entries.title: Dashboard shares: let viewers download widget data as CSV or XLSX
entries.summary: **Allow viewers to download** on a dashboard share link lets anyone opening the shared dashboard download each widget's data as **.CSV** or **.XLSX** — the same rows the widget shows, with the same PII setting, date and time format and 500-row cap, named after the widget. It is off on every existing and new link until you turn it on; a password-protected link asks for the password first, every download is written to the link's access log, and switching it off or revoking the link stops downloads at once. Links with it on show a **Downloads** badge in the Share dialog.

enable.path: Dashboard → Settings → Share → Create New Link → Allow viewers to download

where.path: Shared dashboard page → Download menu on each widget

entries.use_case: Organizers who share live dashboards with clients or stakeholders can now let those viewers download widget data directly, without needing admin access or a separate report share. The toggle is off by default, so existing shares stay view-only until an organizer deliberately enables it.

cs_action.note: Staff turn Allow viewers to download on per share link in the dashboard's Share dialog (super-user control). ICS Events (US) was the originating request and has 2 dashboard shares — reach out once it is on.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Any time a customer says their clients want to download data from a shared dashboard, or when they are using dashboard shares instead of report shares.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers who share dashboards externally with clients, sponsors, or leadership who need offline copies of the data.
internal.staff_path: Dashboard → Settings → Share → link row → Allow viewers to download (super user)
internal.gotchas: The checkbox and the per-link switch are super-user-only in the Share dialog for now (web-ui-v2 #1192); customers see the viewer side (Download menus) once staff turn it on for a link. All 13 existing dashboard shares (12 US, 1 EU) default to off. Downloads are capped at 500 rows (the widget's display limit). There is no 'Download all widgets'; each widget is downloaded individually.
internal.talk_track: If your clients are viewing a shared dashboard and want to take the data away in a spreadsheet, you can now flip a switch on that share link to let them download any widget as CSV or XLSX — same data they see on screen, same formatting, and you can turn it off at any time.

entries.title: Portal: Edit Submission when the form is open, no empty Submission Tasks, and a Show Tasks Widget setting
entries.summary: The button on a portal session now reads **Edit Submission** while the submission form still accepts changes, and **View Submission** once the form has closed or the submission was withdrawn. Portal users who have contact tasks but no submission tasks no longer see an empty **Submission Tasks** section. A new **Show Tasks Widget** setting on the portal's **Configuration** step hides the Tasks card on the portal home and **Tasks** in the portal navigation, the same way the Sessions widget can be hidden.

where.path: Portal → Configuration → Show Tasks Widget; portal home → Tasks card; session → Edit Submission / View Submission

entries.use_case: Speakers who can still edit their submission now see a clearly labelled **Edit Submission** button instead of the ambiguous "View Submission" label, reducing confusion and support requests. Organizers who do not use submission tasks can hide the Tasks widget entirely so the portal home stays clean and relevant for their speakers.

cs_action.note: All three changes are on by default. Show Tasks Widget is on for every existing portal, so nothing disappears until an organizer turns it off.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks why speakers are confused about whether they can edit their submission, or when a customer wants to simplify the portal home for events that don't use submission tasks.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using the speaker/contact portal with submission forms or portal tasks.
internal.staff_path: Event → Portal → Configuration → Show Tasks Widget
internal.gotchas: The Edit Submission label follows the same rules as the submission form itself: form open, not past its last close date, submission not withdrawn, and the form not deleted. A form the organizer deleted still shows View Submission.
internal.talk_track: Speakers told us the 'View Submission' button was confusing — they didn't know they could still edit. Now the button says 'Edit Submission' when the form is open, and 'View Submission' when it's closed. We also cleaned up the Tasks panel so speakers who have no submission tasks don't see an empty section, and gave organizers a toggle to hide the Tasks widget entirely if they don't use it.

entries.title: Put portal pages and files in the order speakers should read them
entries.summary: **Portals → Resources** and **Portals → Files** now have an order of their own. Drag a page or file by its handle, or use **Move up** and **Move down**, and the new order saves at once and applies to every portal of the event, so the onboarding checklist sits first and the venue map last without editing each portal's **Customize → Resources**. Reordering pauses while a search filters the list.

where.path: Program → Portals → Resources / Files (drag handle, Move up, Move down)

entries.use_case: What matters most at the start of speaker onboarding is obsolete a month later. Instead of rebuilding each portal's resource list, the team drags the current priority to the top once and every portal follows.

cs_action.note: On for everyone. The release also backfilled every event's library order from the order its portals already used, so nothing moved on the day.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks why the Resources page lists pages in a strange order (it used to be by title, Z→A) or wants the most important resource shown first.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any event with more than a handful of portal pages or files; Eudēmonia raised it.
internal.staff_path: Event → Portals → Resources or Files → drag handle
internal.gotchas: Needs permission to update portal tasks. The same release lets staff assign pages and files to individual contacts, sessions or groups (checkbox per row, Assign to contacts, sessions or groups, an Everyone / N assigned badge) — super-user-only for now; promote the gate before telling customers. Per-portal Customize → Resources order still works and is re-sequenced to follow the library order.
internal.talk_track: You can now drag your portal resources into the order you want speakers to read them, once, and every portal follows.

entries.title: Weekly portal summary skips people with nothing left to do
entries.summary: The Monday **Weekly Digest Email** now goes only to portal users who still have something outstanding — an incomplete task or form, or a file request with nothing uploaded or a denied upload. When any of a person's items are marked **Required**, only those count. A comment on their session in the last 7 days still sends it, and a denied file reads **Denied - Please Resubmit**. **Send → Send Portal Summary** in Contacts always sends.

where.path: Participants' Monday Weekly Digest Email (portal → Configuration → Portal Notifications → Weekly Digest Email)

entries.use_case: Speakers who have finished everything stop getting a Monday reminder they do not need, so the people who still owe you something are more likely to read theirs.

cs_action.note: Automatic. Expect fewer weekly digest sends on events where most participants are done; that drop is the point of the change.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer or speaker complains about weekly reminders after finishing every task, or asks why weekly digest volume dropped.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every customer with Weekly Digest Email on for a portal.
internal.staff_path: Event → Portals → ⋯ → Preview weekly reminders (staff only) lists exactly who the next Monday run will email.
internal.gotchas: Required-only counting is per person: if none of that person's items are marked Required, every item counts, so optional items still trigger the email. A file waiting for review or approved does not count; a denied file does. A session comment in the last 7 days always sends. The manual Send Portal Summary from Contacts is unchanged and always sends.
internal.talk_track: The weekly digest now only goes to people who still have something to do. If you want to nudge someone anyway, Send Portal Summary from Contacts still sends to anyone you pick.

entries.title: Sort a table from its column header
entries.summary: Open a column header's menu and choose **Sort Ascending**, **Sort Descending** or **Clear Sort** on **Contacts**, **Sessions > Submissions**, **Agenda > List**, **Applications** and the follow-up form, file request and organization portal form submissions tables. The sort shows in the **Sort** panel and marks the view as changed: **Save Changes** keeps it, **Reset Changes** puts the saved sort back.

where.path: Any listed table → column header menu

entries.use_case: Reordering a long contacts or submissions list is one click on the column instead of a trip into the Sort panel.

cs_action.note: On for every admin. Column pinning in the same menu is staff-only for now — do not demo or promise it.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks for a faster way to sort a table, or says sorting from the header 'should just work'.
internal.staff_path: Same as the customer; staff also see Pin column (super users only).
internal.gotchas: A header sort replaces the current sort list with that one column; stacking up to three sorts is still done in the Sort panel. Clear Sort removes only that column. Columns that cannot be sorted show no sort actions. Reset Changes on Sessions and Agenda now restores the saved view's full state.
internal.talk_track: You can now sort any table by clicking its column header — and save the sort with your view.
